candidate_origins.todo_line: - [ ] 003 Introduce and focused-test an app-owned dashboard query/view-model boundary that begins from the authenticated email and fresh active-club authority; move all projection-backed dashboard data behind one coherent socket assign, subscribe before the connected initial read, preserve route/access error semantics and transient LiveView state, and retain the existing notification predicates provisionally.

completion_evidence_required: List every changed path and identify the shared initial/refresh dashboard-installation path, if introduced.
Show the exact `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.page_title/1` assertion and its expected club-specific title including the ` · Memba` suffix.

Confirm by source inspection that top-level `:page_title` is derived only from the newly installed dashboard result on both mount and refresh, with no independent read or additional mirrored projection fields.
Report exact focused validation commands, exit statuses and concise pass summaries.
Report any unresolved issue without marking task 003 complete.
constraints: Keep the task identity `task-003` and preserve the candidate provenance; this is a bounded revision, not a new implementation task.
The top-level `:page_title` must always be derived from the dashboard result being installed and must not come from a separate query, stale selected-club assign or mount-time club snapshot.
Apply the derivation on both initial success and refresh success so future title-changing dashboard results cannot leave shell metadata stale.
Keep `:dashboard` as the sole projection-backed query-result assign; do not restore selected club, selected group, rows, counts, messages or permissions as top-level compatibility mirrors.
Preserve existing `:forbidden` and `:not_found` behavior and all current transient LiveView state.
Use focused deterministic tests and do not use `Process.sleep/1`.
Do not mark the todo line complete; return evidence for review.
outcome: Restore the club-specific browser title while preserving `:dashboard` as the sole projection-query result assign by deriving the LiveView shell's top-level `:page_title` metadata from each successfully installed dashboard result, with focused regression coverage.

references.facts: The latest review accepted the candidate's fresh authority, coherent `:dashboard` result, subscribe-before-read ordering, provisional predicates and transient-state proof, but requires revision because the root layout reads `socket.assigns.page_title`; it specifically requests deriving that shell assign from `dashboard.page_title` and adding a `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.page_title/1` assertion.

The candidate changed the dashboard query, LiveView and focused tests and reported 85 focused tests passing. Those changes remain unaccepted candidate work and must be preserved while addressing the review gap.

Successful mount currently assigns only `:dashboard`, successful `refresh_dashboard/2` replacements also assign only `:dashboard`, and `render/1` expands the dashboard map only into render-local assigns. That expansion is too late to supply LiveView shell metadata.

The root layout's `<.live_title>` reads `assigns[:page_title]`, defaults to `Memba`, and appends ` · Memba`; therefore the LiveView socket must carry the derived top-level title for initial rendering and title diffs.
The coherent dashboard result already contains `page_title: selected_club.name`; this value is the sole permitted source for shell title metadata and no extra club read is needed.

The focused LiveView suite already builds a signed-in routed club dashboard and is the appropriate place to assert `page_title(view) == "Alpine Club · Memba"` while retaining existing route, access and transient-state coverage.

The plan requires one coherent dashboard query result bound to one assign while preserving existing page behavior. Deriving shell metadata from that result does not split the query or authorize an independent read.
ADR 0027 requires club home to begin with one coherent dashboard view model rather than separately refreshed projection fields; the revision must keep `:dashboard` as that one result.
LiveView state changes should be made through socket assigns and focused LiveView tests should assert rendered behavior using the framework's test APIs.

scope: Update the successful initial dashboard installation and every successful dashboard refresh so the socket receives both the coherent `:dashboard` query result and a top-level `:page_title` derived only from `dashboard.page_title`.
Prefer one small installation helper or equivalent shared path so initial mount and refresh cannot diverge; the helper must not perform another read or mirror any other dashboard fields.

Add a focused `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.page_title/1` assertion proving that the routed club dashboard retains its club-specific title, including the root layout suffix, after the single-result-assign migration.

Retain all accepted parts of the existing task-003 candidate: fresh email-based authority, one dashboard result assign, connected subscribe-before-read ordering, current route/access transitions, provisional notification predicates and transient-state preservation.
scope_exclusions: Do not move additional dashboard fields back to top-level socket assigns; `:page_title` is permitted shell metadata, not a second query result.
Do not redesign the root layout or change title text, suffix behavior, dashboard rendering, URLs, DOM structure or user-facing copy.
Do not implement opaque interests, scoped notification translation, bind-time reconciliation, reconnect machinery or subscriber cleanup from tasks 004 and 005.
Do not broaden or otherwise revise the provisional projector predicates.

Do not change conversation detail, another LiveView, the local package, Mix/Docker/quality-gate integration, acceptance features, ADRs, the approved plan, migration matrix, todo file or delivery artifacts.
todo_line: - [ ] 003 Introduce and focused-test an app-owned dashboard query/view-model boundary that begins from the authenticated email and fresh active-club authority; move all projection-backed dashboard data behind one coherent socket assign, subscribe before the connected initial read, preserve route/access error semantics and transient LiveView state, and retain the existing notification predicates provisionally.
